subject.title: [Feature]: Built-in headless browser for reliable web access without external dependencies

question: Should OpenClaw make rendered browser-backed web access a core/default web_fetch or web_search capability, keep it as explicit browser-plugin tooling, or add a narrower plugin/API extension for rendered extraction?
rationale: The implementation path changes public tool semantics, browser packaging, logged-in session handling, proxy behavior, and security boundaries; source inspection cannot choose that product contract safely.

options.title: Approve staged browser-backed extraction design
options.body: Define a gated design for rendered extraction that preserves external-content wrapping, browser SSRF policy, session storage rules, proxy credential handling, and benchmarks before code lands.

options.title: Keep browser explicit for now
options.body: Leave web_fetch and web_search as lightweight/provider tools and document when users should enable the browser tool, Firecrawl, or another provider for JS-heavy or login-required pages.

options.title: Split into narrower trackers
options.body: Route proxy/isolation, cookie persistence, backend packaging, and search/fetch extraction into separate canonical issues, then close or narrow this umbrella after owners agree.

recommendation.title: Approve staged browser-backed extraction design
recommendation.body: Define a gated design for rendered extraction that preserves external-content wrapping, browser SSRF policy, session storage rules, proxy credential handling, and benchmarks before code lands.

likelyOwner.reason: The inspected history shows Peter as the strongest current owner of the browser/web runtime boundary and docs that would define this product shape.
